title: Scripture and Obedience
definition: Scripture and obedience belong together because God's Word is given not only to be heard but to be believed, practiced, and lived.
summary: The faithful hearer does not treat Scripture as information only, but as the voice of the Lord calling for trust and response.
christFocus: Jesus calls His disciples to hear His words and do them, building life on the solid rock of His teaching.

studySections.heading: Doctrine in Summary
studySections.content: Scripture and Obedience teaches that God's people must receive this truth under the authority of the Lord, allowing Scripture itself to define the doctrine rather than personal opinion, tradition, or culture.

studySections.heading: Why This Matters
studySections.content: This doctrine matters because it protects the believer from confusion and helps the church remain anchored in what God has actually spoken. Without this truth, faith can drift toward feelings, assumptions, or human wisdom.

studySections.heading: Discipleship and Application
studySections.content: A disciple should respond to scripture and obedience by reading the Word prayerfully, testing beliefs by Scripture, obeying what God reveals, and helping others handle the Bible with humility, clarity, and faith.

studySections.heading: Guardrails and Common Errors
studySections.content: This doctrine should not be used to win arguments while neglecting love, nor should it be separated from prayer, obedience, and dependence on the Holy Spirit. The goal is faithful submission to God, not mere possession of information.

sources: Scripture references listed in this doctrine entry.
